label: u/w input at step 3 (4th original token) after r/g/l/f/p-type letters
predicate: (t == 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("u"), tok("w")]) & (isin(prev_tok, [tok("r"), tok("g"), tok("l"), tok("f"), tok("p"), tok("y"), tok("z"), tok("j")]) | isin(prev2_tok, [tok("r"), tok("g"), tok("l"), tok("f"), tok("p"), tok("y"), tok("z"), tok("j")]))
explanation: Sparse update-gate unit that fires only in the original phase, at positions 2-4, and 88% of its activation mass is at t=3 (the 4th original token). It never fires at t=0,1 or t>=5, or on the delimiter or copy steps. The input token matters most: u (51% of mass) and w (28%), then b and 0. It is boosted when the one or two tokens just before are r (strongest), g, l, f, p, y, z, or j. The top activations are all of the form ... r [u], e.g. p r r [u], n l r [u]. Almost all activations fall on the first occurrence of the input token. The simpler predicate t==3 & in_tok in {u,w} has mass recall 0.67 but precision 0.28, because u/w at step 3 without the preceding letters mostly stays below threshold. Adding the previous-token condition raises dev F1 to 0.48. Its magnitude looks like a graded combination of position, current token and recent tokens, which a boolean predicate captures only in part.
